chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: How McRae gained responsibility; Chick wanted a hot and smooth tenor
summary: After the first tour McRae took on duties; Chick wanted his Herschel Evans-like style after Elmer Williams.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose

blocks.x: When actually did you gain more responsibility in the orchestra -- Chick Webb's orchestra -- so far as arranging and doing some writing?
When I came back after the first tour --
No. Right around thirty -- After the first tour in '36.
When we first went into the Apollo. Yeah. When we went on in to the Apollo.

Chick always liked me before. He always wanted me for something. I found out what it was when I got over there.
He wanted me for -- because Elmer had left. I was the next smoothest tenor player that he had ever heard outside of Herschel Evans with the Cloud of Joy.
Herschel and I played on the order. same Basie
Dick Wilson (inaudible). is who you're thinking B
Dick Wilson and Herschel, we always played that same beautiful style and could play it hot too, you know.
And Chick wanted me, but Elmer didn't play that. He never played hot tenor, you know. He just played, you know, smooth, you know.
That's what I'm saying, when I joined the band and Chick played like "King Porter Stomp," or something and I was playing.
And Charlie Buchanan stuck his head out and say, "Who's that tenor player you got now?"
